purpose: Screen the major oceanic and small-island archipelago series represented in the plant-pollination/reproductive-biology literature, then separate strict frozen-ABM state-class validation targets from partial mechanism links, filtering/architecture evidence, and unresolved geographic gaps.
scope_boundary: This is a global archipelago screening frame, not a claim that every named island on Earth or every publication has been exhaustively recovered. Continental megarchipelagos and archipelagos without a source-comparable pollination/reproductive chain are retained as screened gaps rather than silently omitted. No absence-of-evidence row is interpreted as evidence that relevant literature does not exist.
search_basis: the nine focal oceanic archipelagos plus broader island-group conservation synthesis
repository source audits and source-locked result registries already present in izu-core
named archipelago and focal-taxon searches performed on 2026-08-24

admission_tiers.A: strict state-class validation target: an external island-system contrast or perturbation reaches a downstream reproductive/floral response and can be classified using the already-frozen ABM state vocabulary without retuning
admission_tiers.B: direct mechanism component or partial propagation chain: useful for constraining support, effectiveness, dependency, replacement, morphology or reproduction, but missing a matched transition link
admission_tiers.C: colonization/filtering, community architecture or macroevolution layer: useful for who reaches/persists on islands or how interaction structure differs, but not a strict ABM propagation-state test
admission_tiers.D: screened geographic gap: no source-comparable chain was recovered in this pass; this is not a claim that no relevant literature exists

Musschia/Echium systems supply pollinator dependence, delayed selfing and multi-guild visitation components; no strict matched transition recovered
Malva and Cneorum quantify insects, birds/lizards, autogamy and reproductive outcomes, but contrasts do not provide a full archipelago transition on one common estimand
island-wide honeybee removal changes floral resource standing crop and wild-pollinator network context; matched plant reproductive response is not measured
Freycinetia and other systems document narrow native vertebrate pollination pathways, including flying foxes/birds, but no comparable pollinator-loss transition was recovered
Scaevola taccada work measures visitor community and pollinator-exclusion reproduction with introduced honeybee dominance; single-island component rather than a matched archipelago transition
endemic Nesohedyotis/Commidendrum studies provide current pollinator and breeding-system specialization/niche divergence; no independent regime transition recovered
community-scale native plant pollination and introduced-honeybee dominance constrain interaction architecture, but no matched functional-loss-to-reproduction contrast was recovered

25 endemic species show very high self-compatibility, rare native insect visitation and strong wind/geitonogamy components; powerful archipelago reproductive-filter evidence but not a matched transition

claim_boundary: Tier A asks only whether an already-frozen qualitative response class can accommodate an external observed state. It does not identify the real-world ABM mechanism. Tier B/C systems must not be forced into state labels to inflate replication. Tier D records search coverage gaps, not biological absence. No common effect-size meta-analysis is licensed by this screen.
